1.why: All eight screens show a static, uncluttered card layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings and solid blue primary buttons stand out clearly against the white form cards on every step.

3.why: Each step has a single clear title and main field, so the next required action is easy to locate quickly.

4.why: The user must recall multi-step sequence details plus the full password complexity rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol).

5.why: No password-manager hooks, autofill prompts, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Fields start empty or show only newly typed values with no saved-account cues or familiar-item recognition aids.

7.why: Labels and instructions are mostly short and plain-language, though a few explanatory sentences run longer.

8.why: No error messages are shown in any screenshot, so none describe problems or fixes.

9.why: Password rules are listed without an example value, and other fields lack sample inputs or format illustrations.

10.why: The flow offers only a fixed password-reset plus MFA-code path; no clear choices among password, code, or face login.

11.why: Most screens present only one or two primary actions, so the user is not flooded with simultaneous choices.

12.why: Outcomes are explicitly confirmed, e.g. the green “reset instructions have been prepared” banner and the final “Conditions accepted” page.

13.why: Short tips appear, including the Stay-safe box, password-requirement text, and notes on where the mock MFA code is delivered.

14.why: A Back button exists on the token step and a return-to-start button at the end, but error-retry paths are not shown.

15.why: Header, card layout, button styles, and logs panel remain visually identical across all eight steps.
